key_insight: Grain-boundary segregation in nanocrystalline Fe-18Cr-12Ni delays the onset of plastic flow, mainly by slowing early deformation through Ni depletion and Cr enrichment at grain boundaries.
engineering_relevance: Tuning grain-boundary chemistry could improve the early-stage strength and deformation resistance of nanocrystalline austenitic alloys across a wide temperature range.
method: Hybrid MD/MC simulations on three independent nanocrystalline Fe-18Cr-12Ni polycrystals
Comparison against annealed and random controls on the same microstructures
Constant-stress and fixed-strain-rate deformation tests at 300–950 K
evidence_signal: At 4.6 GPa and 300 K, segregated polycrystals reached 50% strain about 16% later than random ones, and showed a 6–7% higher peak stress than annealed controls across 300, 750, and 950 K.
watch_item: The measured Cr enrichment depends strongly on the chosen reference region, so composition results should be interpreted carefully when comparing GB and grain-interior definitions.
paper_title: Grain-boundary segregation delays the onset of plastic flow in nanocrystalline Fe-18Cr-12Ni
